title: Google gives US K-12 schools an either-or choice: enable AI search or turn off search
excerpt: According to a Bloomberg report on November 3, Google has tightened access to its services for U.S. K-12 schools. Chris Phillips, head of its education business
content_html:
According to a Bloomberg report on November 3, Google has tightened access to its services for U.S. K-12 schools. Chris Phillips, head of its education business, made it clear: for student accounts from kindergarten through 12th grade, Google Search, the Gemini chatbot, Gemini Notebook, and Gemini features in Google Classroom are all turned off by default and must be manually enabled by school administrators. In other words, the Search switch is in administrators' hands—but once Search is turned on, the embedded AI capabilities are enabled along with it.

Pushback from Parents and Districts Forces This "Single-Choice Question"
